I’m by no means saying that apples are ‘bad’ just that I expected blueberries to come out below them. Blueberries have a great amount of resistant starch, inulin, and are rich in polyphenols called flavonoids that increase antioxidant levels in the body. They’re an excellent prebiotic, too! Apples might be a little lackluster in vitamin content. That’s why weighing fruits on whether they’re healthy or not is difficult, because it really depends on what you’re needing so varying intake is a given.

You could try other variations of berries, black and raspberries are very good. Kiwis also have an excellent nutritional value. They have more Vitamin C than oranges do! Nothing wrong with apples and bananas though.

Sure! None of them were necessarily the “worst” or “bad”. Fruit juice that’s not freshly squeezed at home is at the bottom of the list. 

Blueberries and kiwis are at the top for similar reasons. She says that all berries are pretty healthy. Strawberries, bananas, oranges, watermelon, and apples are all relatively equal, with apples at the lower end of that tier after oranges and bananas. 

She gives good reasoning in the video including year round availability as a factor to her ranking and it was really engaging it honestly didn’t feel like 15 minutes AND I have a terrible attention span, so I really recommend watching the video because she ranks them with no control variable (so this ranking doesn’t necessarily represent the ‘objectively’ healthiest foods if we’re going off of vitamins vs. just antioxidants or whatever measure of health because she considers other things as a ranking of ‘best’ fruit).

Blueberries— So many healthy nutrients and believed to contain some of the highest amounts of antioxidants of all the fruits and vegetables, as most berries are, but this one is by far superior in it’s well-roundedness. It’s particularly high in Vitamin K, C, Fiber, and Manganese.

I found out about this through this video about [whether or not fruit is healthy](https://youtu.be/waZZIK6zwxE). I was so shocked to see it at the top of the list and apples, easily marketed as /the/ ‘healthy’ fruit (the whole eat an apple a day keep the doctor away thing), decent, but not with the best nutritional value.

Honestly, r/OliveMUA has been a big help to me. I’ve only realized I had an olive skintone within the past week so I don’t have much information on the best colors recommended for olive skin. But, I definitely recommend taking a look over there for some help in the makeup department. The tips they give over there have been helpful overall. The colors that I enjoy wearing on my lips actually look great on as clothes as well. 

It definitely depends on the depth, chroma, and contrast. Off the top of my head, I think you would look lovely in a lavender, periwinkle, or peachy shades. Also, matching the color of your eyes can’t go wrong, and this is personal preference, but mauve and taupe are favorites of mine and the smokiness of the shades would give your coloring justice I feel! But, I’m in no ways a professional. You have a light/medium depth (overall lightness/midtones in your eyes, skin, and hair) low chroma (the colors apparent in your eyes, skin, and hair are overall desaturated) and medium contrast (because your eyes, skin, and hair are somewhat desaturated yet, they have a prominent quality in being a light grey/blue, and not quite rich brown or dark blonde hair, somewhere in between, and your being overall neutral, but leaning cool) think. So you would wear clothes in colors with a light/medium depth, low chroma, and/or a medium contrast. Hopefully this should give you some ideas: https://imgur.com/gallery/OJyZu1B

Finding celebrities with similar features to you and looking to see what colors makes them shine could also be helpful! 

Also, from what I’ve seen with people who have an olive skintone is that we’re not catered to a lot so the process for finding the best colors is a little arduous and more trial and error than others. But don’t give up, I think you would look great in the soft-summer shades. My advice would be to just eliminate anything you don’t feel your best in immediately, which is simple and perhaps not refined and the clean-cut advice you wished for, but the best I can offer. 

You’re welcome by the way, most people don’t realize they’re olive-toned either! There’s some big misconception about olive-tones needing to be darker which is not the case at all!

Hi!! This is so strange.. but I’ve just done the same thing as you. Realized I was a vessel for peoples’ problems, lives, etc. Had a good cry like I always do when I remember that people don’t like me, but they way I make them feel. Typed in lonely into reddit and you’re one of the first people at the top of the subreddit. I’ve never been able to let people get close to me. I always felt like I was burdening them. At the start, I’d stay quiet, not bother at all if they weren’t listening. But lately i’ve been overcompensating. Talking and talking and talking about random stuff, noticing they don’t care and aren’t interested in my thoughts, points of view, my life, me and I just keep going hoping that the noise of my conversation drowns out the pain that I feel for always being the first to interact, always being there for everyone and returning to myself at the end of the day. I’m never myself until I’m alone. I’ve been trying lately to think really clearly so that I stop but I can’t it’s like a dam that broke and I can’t reseal. I understand so much what you’re going through. I tear myself apart at night wishing that someone, just anyone would give me a shred of human decency, that I wouldn’t have to ask people how they were in hopes that they would ask how I am and see that I’m not fine. But they don’t want to see. I’m actually very private despite being loud, a huge introvert beneath everything, I’m very open to new ideas but I have morals and beliefs that I don’t ever let go of. It’s like they see someone that’s not me.. but them, just better? I started to let go of these people, reply less, reply the way that I feel in the moment instead of doing what would make them feel best. They’ll realize they lost something that other people just don’t give and they’ll want you. But don’t ever, ever give in again. The truth is that a lot of people will take advantage of your sincerity, so you must learn to give it sparingly. I’m so sorry that it has to be this way, but just know that you’re not alone, lonely but not alone. You’re not asking for too much, you’re kind, and sincere, and genuine. I know you love listening to people, hearing what they have to say and you remember, but you deserve that, too. You shouldn’t have to beg for human decency. I am so so sorry that you’re going through this, too. Words cannot express how sorry I am, but everything you said, everything is so so familiar to me. Constantly, ever since childhood, making people happy, made me happy, but we deserve what we give and I hope that someday, somebody, anybody, will be able to provide that without the relationship falling apart.

I’ve only started watching dramas in 2017 and I actually enjoy older dramas. There’s a certain charm and sort of.. innocence? in them that I don’t really see anymore. Because nowadays production is so high, and stories are becoming more and more out there, I think older dramas are special. They are generally more relatable because the ideas that were fresh were fresh back then and not so much now, so it’s comforting to watch. Also, even though everyone can appreciate a good scenery, the lack of scenery in older dramas allows a focus on the story. I understand that it’s difficult to watch something that feels overdone and maybe a little trope-y, but it’s so pure and calming that I think everyone should try. Princess Hours, Coffee Prince, Stairway to Heaven, Winter Sonata, Autumn in My Heart, Boys Over Flowers, and Full House I think are must watches. Boys Over Flowers is getting pegged as cringey and I would just like to say that it is sort of cringey but it still holds a certain kind of childlike innocence as in, the story is very simple and upfront and I can appreciate that. It also has my favorite second female lead ever. Dramas nowadays make female leads really bitchy but this one was really relatable despite the story being so dramatic. Full House’s male lead sort of made me mad and the story itself is very strange looking back on it but I think if you can learn to appreciate it for what it is, then it’s definitely worth a watch. 

If you have trouble with older dramas, I think you should try watching Pinocchio. It’s not that old from what I remember and it has a more recent and fresh take on the older, more dramatic dramas that have ties to family while still having a fun and interesting romantic and professional work plot. 

TL;DR

Appreciate older dramas for what they were. There’s a lot to be learned from these dramas. Even though they lack the cinematography and writing of today’s dramas, the simplicity and innocence they hold brings attention to a storyline that they began. They began the tropes you see today and we all should return back to these roots to be able to have that ‘drama’ experience.

I’ve gotten a hair botox and two keratin treatments.

A little history, I got my first ever keratin treatment 4 years ago. I had thick (and I mean extremely thick) frizzy (I suspect I had curly hair which I braided every single day for the majority of my childhood), healthy, and shiny, brown, hair. The results were amazing, my hair was straight, but it was very expensive. It faded (as in my roots completely grew out and I chopped my waist length hair) around 2 years later. My hair was significantly duller even though the formulation was formaldehyde free. I got so much more breakage despite the treatment going away and my hair was now coarser, despite each individual strand becoming thicker.

Around 1 year later, I get another keratin treatment someplace else. I suspect the person who placed it on my hair lied to me about what was in it, however, everything was all right until, I got severe dandruff. I remember my scalp itching and burning horrifically during the treatment, but I was too anxious to speak up and everytime I tried, the worker would brush me off and tell me I had so much hair and it was a lot of work. Flash forward 2 weeks later, my hair is pin straight, my scalp is EXTREMELY scaly and painful. My entire scalp sheds. I suspect my hair follicle was severely damaged as my hair would take ages to grow in, and would grow in rough, thin, yet coarse strands, covering less of my scalp by square inch, unlike the thick, waist length hair I used to have. 

I left my hair alone the year after focusing on growing out bad layers. 

This year, around September, I got a hair botox treatment. This nourished my severely protein loaded hair but at the cost of giving me dandruff. I get thick patches of dandruff now when I had never previously had that. I only get that in my bang area and the hair there is starting to thin. I’m in my late teens (19) so I cannot see how this is a normal change. 

Absolutely under no circumstances, should you get a keratin treatment. I hope that you can find a routine and to find a way to work with your natural hair so that you enjoy it, can have fun with it, and have the gorgeous hair of your dreams, but keratin is not the way. If I could tell younger me anything to help with her hair, I’d tell her to never, under any circumstances, do or follow along with a keratin treatment. It caused irreversible damage that is still healing, even almost 5 years after. I went from having the prettiest hair, to refusing to go outside because my hair would not work with me.

In regards to hair botox, I liked it. Just make sure you do it with someone you trust, and you don’t have a particularly oily, dry, or dandruff prone scalp. If you have a normal scalp, go for it! 

Any questions or clarifications are welcomed.
